name: clinical_guideline_graph
description: Layer 2 of the KG-XAI knowledge graph: the formalized decision chain (deck Objective 1). Concept nodes are the quantities the model outputs or the dataset provides; eligibility rules come from trial and guideline criteria; plausibility constraints encode which JOINT outputs are clinically coherent -- those drive the consistency loss and JDCR (deck Problem Statement).

isles24_data.citation: This project's own measurements on the ISLES'24 public training release (outputs/tables/kg_node_features.json, clinical_completeness.json).

concept_nodes.availability_note: Replaces binary LVO yes/no: only 4/149 subjects have an empty lvo-msk, so a binary head would have 4 negatives. Classes from confidence-gated occlusion site: proximal_anterior = confident ICA/MCA (87), other_confident = confident ACA/PCA/BA (15), distal_unlocalized (42), none (4). Final label scheme set in Phase 2.
Side of the occluded vessel. Low-confidence cases still carry reliable side: 17/17 low-confidence anterior cases matched the infarct side.

ISLES'24 ships no collateral grade. Proxy = HIR = volume(Tmax>10s) / volume(Tmax>6s). HIGH HIR = POOR collaterals (Olivot 2014: 'A high HIR predicted poor collaterals with an area under the curve of 0.73'). Built in Phase 2; always reported as a proxy.
What H1 predicts and what ISLES'24 labels (lesion-msk, follow-up DWI day 2-9). NOT the same quantity as the trials' admission core.
Side holding the majority of infarct voxels, relative to the vessel-pair midline (src/graph/features.py).

The trials' 'core' is tissue already infarcted at admission, measured on perfusion/diffusion imaging. Planned derivation: relative CBF < 30% on the CBF map. The exact method each trial used must be confirmed in Phase 2 before claiming equivalence.
Hypoperfused tissue, Tmax > 6 s (the same threshold HIR's denominator uses).
ASPECTS is a CT region score. Not provided by ISLES'24. The AHA/ASA 2026 rules are written in ASPECTS, so they cannot be evaluated here; the trial rules are written in mL and can.
90/149 filled -- rules needing it are indeterminate for the other 59
148/149 filled. Says onset time is unknown; does not give the time window.

Every timing column in the release (Onset to door, Alert to door, Door to imaging, Door to groin, Door to first series, Door to recanalization, Time of intervention) is empty for all 149 subjects. No time-window condition can be evaluated.

eligibility_rules.note: Observational evidence, not a guideline rule. The same study reports benefit in the 50-110 mL range, so large core alone is not an exclusion.

plausibility_constraints.statement: The infarct should be on the same side as the occluded vessel.
plausibility_constraints.clinical_basis: Arterial occlusion causes ischemia in the territory the artery supplies, which is ipsilateral for the ICA, MCA, ACA and PCA.

support.evidence: Ground truth, confident anterior-circulation cases: 89/94 (94.7%) same side. Confident PCA: 6/6. Low-confidence anterior: 17/17.
support.why_soft: Real data violates it 5.3% of the time (2 near-midline ACA cases, 1 bilateral infarct, 2 unexplained -- flagged for review). A hard constraint would penalise the model for matching the ground truth.

plausibility_constraints.statement: With a proximal occlusion, good collaterals should not co-occur with a very large final infarct.
plausibility_constraints.clinical_basis: Olivot 2014: 'Initial infarct growth velocity and total infarct growth were greater among patients with a high HIR' -- i.e. poor collaterals grow larger infarcts; good collaterals, the reverse. This is the cross-task incoherence the deck's Problem Statement names.

support.evidence: Needs the HIR proxy (Phase 2). Volume threshold deliberately NOT set here -- it is chosen from the training-fold distribution, not asserted.

plausibility_constraints.statement: With a proximal occlusion, poor collaterals should not co-occur with a near-zero final infarct.
plausibility_constraints.clinical_basis: Mirror of the constraint above; same source.

support.evidence: Needs the HIR proxy (Phase 2). Caveat: every ISLES'24 patient was successfully reperfused, which limits infarct growth -- this constraint may turn out weak here, and that gets reported.

plausibility_constraints.statement: A clot in a large upstream vessel (ICA/M1) should come with a larger final infarct than a distal clot.
plausibility_constraints.clinical_basis: An upstream occlusion cuts off a larger arterial territory.

support.evidence: Ground truth: proximal median 13.8 mL (n=87) vs distal 13.1 mL (n=42); one-sided Mann-Whitney p=0.66, AUC 0.478. Pass mark (higher median and p<0.05) fixed before running. outputs/tables/constraint_support.json
support.likely_reason: All ISLES'24 patients were successfully reperfused, so final infarct SIZE reflects how fast flow returned more than where the clot sat. Partly also label noise: 11/42 'distal' cases have the clot-side MCA/ICA missing from cow-msk and may be upstream clots in an unopacified vessel.
support.decision: Excluded from JDCR and the consistency loss. Kept on record as a tested-and-rejected candidate. ICA > MCA (p=0.035, one of two unplanned secondary tests, not significant after correction) is a lead to re-test on training folds in Phase 2.

plausibility_constraints.statement: A very large final infarct should not co-occur with 'no occlusion'.
plausibility_constraints.clinical_basis: Large territorial infarcts are driven by large-vessel occlusion.

support.evidence: Only 4/149 subjects have no annotated occlusion -- too few to check the relation. Excluded from JDCR and the consistency loss by default; kept so the graph is complete if more data is added.
